title: AWS re:Invent 2025 - UC San Diego Health modernizes patient engagement with Amazon Connect Customer
headline: UC San Diego Health saves 300,000+ staff hours with AI-powered patient engagement
summary: UCSD Health leverages Amazon Connect and agentic AI to automate patient scheduling and verification, boosting efficiency and patient satisfaction.
operator: Katrina Bidwell (Operations Director, UC San Diego Health)
gradeRationale: Named customer operator (UC San Diego Health) with quantified outcomes; presented at a vendor event.
insights: Agentic AI enables healthcare organizations to automate high-volume, routine patient interactions, freeing staff for more complex care.
Unified cloud-based contact centers integrated with EHRs improve patient experience, operational efficiency, and data-driven decision-making.
Adoption of AI in healthcare is accelerating, with measurable impacts on service levels, staff utilization, and patient satisfaction.
approach: AI agents automate patient verification, appointment scheduling, rescheduling, and information retrieval, integrating with Epic EHR to provide seamless, self-service experiences.

enablingTech.label: Amazon Connect and Epic EHR Integration
enablingTech.text: Cloud-based contact center platform integrated with Epic EHR via real-time APIs, leveraging AWS KMS for security and Contact Lens for analytics.

orgPrereq: Transitioning to agentic AI and unified contact center platforms requires cross-functional collaboration, new skillsets, and a shift toward data-driven, patient-centric operations, enabling scalability and agility.
whyItMatters: Implementing agentic AI in Amazon Connect enables healthcare organizations to reduce operational costs, improve service levels, and deliver a more seamless, patient-centric experience, building trust and loyalty while freeing staff for higher-value tasks.

owner.role: Leads care navigation and contact center transformation
owner.context: Responsible for improving patient engagement and operational efficiency

pitfalls.label: Integration Complexity and Change Management
pitfalls.text: Implementing unified AI-driven systems requires overcoming legacy infrastructure, ensuring data security, and managing organizational change.

quotes.quote: Healthcare is where tech comes to die. And then we revive it.
quotes.speaker: Katrina Bidwell

quotes.quote: When the contact center is already handling more and more of these patient interactions, it stops being just a contact center and it becomes that front door to care.
quotes.speaker: Chris Rollo

roi.formula: ROI = (hours saved x fully-loaded hourly cost) - (platform usage + integration build + ongoing ops)
roi.missing: Build and run cost were not disclosed, so a true ROI cannot be computed from this source
roi.claimed_benefit: 300,000+ staff hours saved in the first year; the operator framed this as the cost of fully-benefited FTE hours

cost.note: UC San Diego Health did not disclose spend.
drivers: Platform usage: Amazon Connect is usage-based (per voice minute and per message), no upfront licence; pricing is public
EHR integration build: Epic API work via internal engineering or a systems integrator, usually the largest line item
Ongoing operations: tuning, monitoring, and prompt/model upkeep

enrichment.provenance: FieldNote analyst layer: market context, cost/ROI framework, readiness and metric definitions, compiled from the record plus general category knowledge and public vendor pricing. Not the deployer words unless quoted.

Clean, current patient and scheduling data

HIPAA and PHI controls (encryption at rest and in transit)

enrichment.time_to_value: Benefits reported within the first year of implementation

metric_definitions.means: Share of patients who completed identity and appointment verification via the AI without a human. A deflection-style metric; it does not by itself mean the underlying problem was resolved.
A labor-efficiency metric, not a care-quality or resolution metric. Its value depends on the fully-loaded hourly cost you assign.
Fewer callers who hung up before being served. An access metric; pair it with resolution and CSAT to judge quality.
